blurb: Large, all-white Argentine mastiff-type dog bred to hunt boar and puma
description: The Dogo Argentino is a large mastiff-type dog from Córdoba, Argentina, with a short all-white coat, bred in the 1920s for hunting big game.
answer: The Dogo Argentino is a large Argentine dog of mastiff type, bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, central Argentina, mainly for hunting big game such as peccaries, wild boar and pumas. It is powerfully built, with a short coat that is always white.

body: In the 1920s Antonio Nores Martinez and his brother Augustin set out to create a big-game hunting dog. Starting from a Bull Terrier bitch and a fighting dog of bulldog type, Antonio selected for a white coat and introduced a Pyrenean Mastiff in the eighth generation; by the twelfth his dogs bred true. Later crosses included the Irish Wolfhound, Boxer, Great Dane and Dogue de Bordeaux. The breed was presented in Buenos Aires in 1947, a standard was published in 1948, and the FCI definitively accepted it in 1973.

Dogs weigh about 40–45 kg, with bitches slightly less; dogs stand 60–68 cm and bitches 60–65 cm at the withers. The body is slightly longer than it is tall. The coat is short and always white; a single dark spot on the head is tolerated if it covers no more than a tenth of the head. The muzzle is about as long as the skull.

The source text gives little detail on temperament. The breed is described as having a good nose, speed and stamina for hunting, and breed club descriptions are the best guide to the character of individual dogs.

Sources give little detail on daily care. The Dogo is kept mainly for hunting and is occasionally trained for police or military work. Ownership of the breed is illegal or restricted in a number of countries, including the United Kingdom, Australia and Norway.

Conditions reported in the breed include congenital deafness and laryngeal paralysis/polyneuropathy complex. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups. The dogs usually live for some 10 to 12 years.

faq.q: How big does a Dogo Argentino get?
faq.a: Dogos are large dogs, standing about 60–68 cm and weighing roughly 40–45 kg, with bitches slightly smaller.

faq.q: What was the Dogo Argentino bred for?
faq.a: It was bred in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting large game such as peccaries, wild boar and pumas.

faq.q: How long do Dogo Argentinos live?
faq.a: The dogs usually live for some 10 to 12 years.

faq.q: Is the Dogo Argentino recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 292 in Group 2.
